AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: This study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of parecoxib injection in pain relief after laparoscopic surgeries.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Comprehensive literature search based on four online databases (Pubmed, EMBASE, CENTRAL, ISI Web of Science) was applied to retrieve all related randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Two independent reviewers screened each article for eligibility according to the predetermined inclusion criteria. The Cochrane's Tool was applied to evaluate the methodological quality of included studies. A standardized data collection sheet was designed to extract data from included studies. RevMan 5.3 was selected to perform meta-analysis.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: A total of 1060 participants that scheduled for gynecological laparoscope or laparoscopic cholecystectomy (LC) were enrolled in 12 selected RCTs. The methodological qualities of studies were evaluated as moderate to high. The combined data showed that perioperative parecoxib injection could significantly reduce the percentage of patients who required adjuvant pain relieve after laparoscopic surgeries. Significantly lower pain score in parecoxib groups was observed which proved that preoperative or intraoperative injection of 40mg parecoxib was more effective than placebo in immediate pain relief after LC. But preoperative injection of 40mg parecoxib showed no improvement compared with placebo in the management of immediate pain following gynecological laparoscope. The occurrence of adverse events showed no differences between perioperative parecoxib administration and placebo control.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Perioperative parecoxib administration is effective in reducing the percentage of patients that acquired adjuvant pain relieve after laparoscopic surgeries without significant evaluated adverse events incident compared with placebo. The effect of parecoxib injection in immediate pain relief remains conflicting. Future RCTs with larger sample size are encouraged. This article is protected by copyright. All rights reserved.
